answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every new identity through one narrow inlet of costly, verifiable work. A newcomer first completes small tasks checked by unrelated peers, and only then gains access to a haven of higher-value jobs; each successful job raises its reputation a little, creating an upward spiral that is cheap to maintain for a real agent but expensive to fake at scale. Clusters that always endorse each other, share timing, or reuse the same phrasing are flagged and cut off together, so mass fake identities cost far more than they can earn.
